text: Can a bound pair travel in the committed slot architecture, with every slot streaming, under the committed schedule?
description:
OP-12: moving binding in the slot architecture.

Known: the committed orientation is an open half-space, 1 of the 192 of 4,096 that are (E-FRC-0130). Waiting slots are exact but cannot pay (E-FRC-0132). A bouncing crossing binds and the pair is stuck, 0.7 docks in 600 beats against 34 (E-FRC-0133). Steering on a round robin of all 11 line matchings frees it: 510 of 576 headings give a bound pair that travels (E-FRC-0146, E-FRC-0147), against 88 of 576 on the committed couples. Folded into the 24-beat palindrome, the round robin reaches all 66 pairs of lines and keeps CPT, and a cold meson travels 20 bound on it (E-FRC-0152, E-FRC-0153). But the fold fails the acceptance battery, a lone vibe's disturbance growing about tenfold each period (E-FRC-0156), and no steering closes the baryon gap while the meson walks (E-FRC-0157). The adopted knit cannot bind either: its positions are classical, and two vibes cost exactly 2 over the vacuum at every separation (E-SPN-0068). On stand-in tokens with amplitudes, only a counted string binds in discrete time, a phase string cannot (E-SPN-0074), and with the store as the flux's own column count the lightest charge-one state is three locked loves, spin one half, compact and travelling (E-SPN-0075 to E-SPN-0078).

Unknown: binding on the knit's own tokens in 3D, which needs the doublet-locked stream (adopted 2026-09-26, not built) and a husk-local home for the string's count (E-SPN-0081).

Why it matters: binding on the D4 lattice is shown only with matter that waits in docks or a new schedule.

Scope: a computational search, then the acceptance battery.

Skills: cellular automata, lattice gauge theory.

Where to start: test/experiment/gauge/steered-binding.ts; test/experiment/gauge/slot-binding.ts.

The claims it would move: R-FRC-0006.

Evidence named: E-FRC-0130, E-FRC-0132, E-FRC-0133, E-FRC-0146, E-FRC-0147, E-FRC-0152, E-FRC-0153, E-FRC-0156, E-FRC-0157, E-SPN-0068, E-SPN-0074 to E-SPN-0078, E-SPN-0081.
